correctness.rationale: The six prism-vertex signs are s_j±t with Σs_j=0 and t=h|n_z|/2. Classifying k=0,1,2,3 crossed vertical edges yields N=4,5,4,3 for all generic normals, excluding measure-zero vertex/edge coincidences. N=3 corresponds exactly to a centered hexagonal cone. The six congruent spherical triangle solid angles give T(h)=6 arctan[h²/(sqrt(3)(4+h²+4sqrt(1+h²/3)))]/π. Each of nine spatial edges is sign-separated with chance θ/π; summing 6 horizontal and 3 vertical contributions proves L(h)=E[N]. The three-point support and two moments yield the remaining probabilities and both height limits. Independently sampled 30,000 random normals at each of h=0.2,1,2,5 and enumerated actual nine edge crossings; results agree with the evaluated probability triple within sampling error. Monte Carlo only corroborates, not proves, the all-height continuum identity.
